intro: This is Topkapı Palace, in İstanbul province, dating from the 1460s. It was built not as a single building but as a compound, growing around four courtyards, and from here the Ottomans ruled for four centuries.
history: After the conquest, Mehmed II set his palace on the point where the Marmara, the Bosphorus and the Golden Horn meet. Topkapı is not one building but a compound of kiosks, dormitories and service blocks strung along four courtyards. As you move inward, access narrows court by court, until the fourth court, open only to the sultan and his closest circle. The palace served until the court moved to Dolmabahçe in the nineteenth century.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Gate of Salutation, the Harem and the Treasury. Seek out the Sacred Relics and the Baghdad Kiosk too, and save some time for the Palace kitchens.
facts: Did you know? The palace kitchens fed close to five thousand people a day; their chimneys were redesigned by Sinan, and today the buildings hold the collection of Chinese porcelain. The palace is a compound rather than a building: four courtyards deep, each admitting fewer people than the last, until the fourth, reserved for the sultan and his closest circle. And look closely at the İznik tiles of the Harem: they carry the coral red that was lost in the sixteenth century and never reproduced.
outro: This brings our tour of Topkapı Palace to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking these courtyards with us, and enjoy the rest of your visit.
